scope: Isolated PostgreSQL HTTP qualification of explicit dated public-website snapshots. No production mutation or chain policy changes.

red.expected_failure: Verified public catalogue lacked site_snapshot metadata before implementation

assertions: A background proof process is confirmed started and blocked before timing the HTTP request
A dated verified website snapshot returns HTTP200 in under500ms while fresh proof is blocked
The snapshot request starts zero additional proof processes
The new head remains unprojected and strict HTTP returns503
Explicit /api/native/public remains strict even with site_snapshot=1
Snapshot metadata identifies verification time, pending refresh and authoritative:false
Every prewarmed public list, stats, map and project subresource returns a verified snapshot
25-row project task subresource retains complete rows and returns page2 with count25 and5rows
Expired snapshots refuse, and a same-generation completed strict recovery warm repopulates them
Changed verifier pin and SQL archive restoration immediately invalidate the snapshot
Missing and archived strict project subresources preserve404
Task discovery and individual task details cannot use dated snapshots
Actual PostgreSQL acquisition, advisory-lock contention, SQL cancellation and cleanup regressions remain green

fences: Current nonretired SQL epoch and matching chain identity
Fresh SQL archive visibility version on each delivery
retention.verification_time: Completed strict proof build, verified strict cache read, or successful background re-verification of the identical generation. HTTP snapshot delivery never renews verification time.
retention.refresh: Existing single-flight five-second background warm, with no request-triggered chain proof work. Cold replicas prewarm all public catalogue paths, each current project, and its tasks/claims/members before readiness.

strict_detail_optimization: Individual task and contribution details skip broad all-record warming. Record resolution, native checkpoint, metadata/body commitments and closure checks remain independently proved.
command: npm run build && node --test --test-concurrency=1 test/native-public-site-snapshot-cache.test.mjs test/native-public-site-snapshot.test.mjs test/native-public-performance.test.mjs test/native-public-catch-up.test.mjs test/native-state-cancellation.test.mjs test/native-catch-up-locks.test.mjs

runtime.database: Shared test-only PostgreSQL localhost55433; tests create and remove their own isolated databases

limitations: Snapshots are explicitly dated website presentation and can be up to120seconds old. They are not current authority for commands, receipts, balances, membership profiles or task discovery.

Production-sized fresh proof rebuild work remains in the background. This fixture proves that such proof work is absent from the opted-in HTTP critical path; production browser/load acceptance is separate.
Snapshot misses, expiry, changed pins, retired epochs and archive visibility changes fail quickly with503 rather than inventing content.

installed_native_e2e.timing_note: Starts after installed worker native run has completed receipt finality and publication; not the first chain receipt timestamp. No explicit projector call occurs after the new submit before HTTP200.
assertions: Actual installed client local MCP signed command succeeds
Receipt finality and exact evidence publication succeed
New strict contribution detail independently proves exact submitted body and exact finalized event cursor
Duplicate native command intent remains idempotent
Contribution attribution and retrieval survive native node restart
installed_native_e2e.runtime: Capped node22 container; existing trusted native daemon and verifier mounted read-only; isolated capped ephemeral pgvector localhost55435 removed after test
installed_native_e2e.note: Existing post-close rate-limit pooled-query warning logged without test failure; no runtime changes were made for it.
